newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strikes disrupt French trains, threaten flights.
newsitem.headline: Strikes disrupt French trains, threaten flights.

text.p: France's SNCF state railway company opened talks on Thursday night with striking train drivers threatening to ruin a busy holiday weekend for tens of thousands, while airline pilots voted to walk out for four days from Tuesday.
SNCF said rail traffic would be heavily disrupted on Friday, which was to be the last day of the three-day stoppage over bonuses and planned job cuts.
But many controllers' assemblies in various parts of the country voted to continue the protest, threatening misery for travellers planning a long weekend extending to Monday, a bank holiday.
SNCF said Eurostar high-speed trains between Paris and London through the Channel tunnel would run normally on Friday.
But services were cut by about a third on other high-speed TGV and regional lines across France, SNCF said.
SNCF management had earlier said it could not improve its terms because of financial constraints and the need to preserve fairness among the company's staff.

Separately six pilot unions at state-owned airlines Air France and its short-haul affiliate Air Inter Europe, formerly Air Inter, announced their intention to resume next Tuesday a strike begun last month after talks with management broke down.
The strike is to protest against planned wage cuts and changes in working conditions under a merger between the European airline and its international parent.
But the Air France group plans to maintain almost all its flights during the strike, as it believes the majority of pilots oppose the stoppage.
"The management will do its utmost to ensure most of the flights will go ahead during the four days," an Air France spokeswoman said.
The pilots decided to renew the strike after talks on Wednesday ended in disagreement, a union official said.

The Air France group decided on Thursday to postpone any decision on pilots' work conditions until the end of June and called on the unions to take advantage of the time to discuss the issue and other matters, the company said in a statement.
